items.title: Boluda buys Dutch offshore towage specialist
points: Spanish towage giant Boluda has acquired Dutch offshore towage and heavy transport specialist Muller Dordrecht, adding 16 tugs and eight barges to its growing global fleet.

The takeover gives Boluda full ownership of the century-old family business, whose fleet includes seven offshore tugs specialising in complex marine transportation, rig moves, anchor handling and offshore wind projects.

Muller, founded in 1918 and headquartered in Dordrecht, will continue operating as an independent unit under the name Boluda Muller Towage, retaining its existing management team and focusing on offshore towage and marine projects worldwide.

The Dutch operator has built a sizeable presence in the North Sea and Baltic markets, supporting offshore energy and infrastructure projects ranging from transporting wind turbine foundations and offshore substations to heavy lifting and coastal towage.
Its fleet includes the 120-tonne bollard pull En Avant 30 and the 90-tonne bollard pull En Avant 25 and En Avant 26, which can operate both offshore and in ports.

The dispute has been running since March and moved into arbitration in London in June, when Hunter initiated proceedings before the London Maritime Arbitrators Association (LMAA) after unpaid hire reached about $28.2m.

items.title: 19 Indian Seafarers Stranded In Yemen For 2 Weeks Evacuated And Heading Home

items.title: 2 teenage girls found hanging from tree in Shahjahanpur village, cops search for their phones
points: The bodies of two teenage girls, aged 17 and 15, were found hanging from a tree in a village in Uttar Pradesh’s Shahjahanpur district on Monday morning.
Shahjahanpur circle officer (Sadar) Shubham Verma said the two girls were close friends and police were gathering information to ascertain the circumstances around their deaths.
The bodies have been sent for postmortem examination, he said.

The incident came to light around 8 am in Haraiya village, under the jurisdiction of the Nigohi police station, when villagers spotted the two close friends hanging from separate dupattas tied to the same branch.
The deceased belonged to the same community and lived in houses roughly 200 metres apart in the same neighbourhood.
Police said they were trying to trace the two teenagers’ mobile phones.
Police would also examine their call records and other available digital evidence during the investigation.
Their families have not levelled any allegations so far.

items.title: Bar licences will not be renewed for hotels denied star classification: Excise Minister
points: Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam Excise Minister M Liju on Monday said bar licences would not be renewed for hotels whose applications for star classification had been rejected by the Union Tourism Ministry.
The state government would also take the same stand before the Kerala High Court in cases pending before it, he said.
He was speaking to reporters amid queries over bar licences being issued to some hotels whose applications for star classification were still pending before the Union Ministry.
Explaining the issue, Liju said a star classification was mandatory for renewing bar licences and the classification was granted by the Union Tourism Ministry.

However, since the Covid-19 pandemic, there had been delays in processing applications for star classification, forcing the state government to renew bar licences with the approval of the state Tourism Department, he said.
The minister said he had directed officials to obtain a list of hotels whose applications for renewal of star classification had been rejected by the Union Tourism Ministry.

At the beginning of the summer, Splash reported that a rusty, 333 m long crude oil tanker with one of the more colourful recent histories in the shadow fleet appeared to be moving towards its endgame.
The 2002-built VLCC Era, better known until recently as Marinera and before that Bella 1, had resurfaced under the Comoros flag after another change of identity.
Sources say it was sold at a huge discount by the US for $205 per ldt.

'Semantically ignorant': Congress defends Kharge's 'Diwali a khushiyon ki Eid' remark
points: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge stirred controversy by referring to Diwali as 'khushiyon ka Eid'.
BJP officials accused the Congress of misrepresenting Diwali, asserting each festival has its unique identity.

Pawan Khera of Congress defended Kharge's statement, emphasizing the meaning of 'Eid' as 'festival.' The BJP responded by questioning the appropriateness of comparing Diwali with Eid, which they deemed disrespectful.
This disagreement highlights ongoing political tensions regarding religious and cultural identities.
